sections.Kurzabstract: The BFAS-G is the German translation of the Big Five Aspect Scale developed by DeYoung and colleagues (2007). The adapted BFAS-G is a self-assessment inventory with 100 items for assessing the Big Five as well as ten underlying aspects (aspects in brackets): (1) Extraversion (assertiveness & enthusiasm), (2) Neuroticism (volatility & withdrawal), (3) Agreeableness (compassion & politeness), (4) Conscientiousness (orderliness & industriousness), (5) Intellect/Openness (intellect & openness). Reliability: Cronbach's alpha is .71 to .91. Validity: The convergent validity with the NEO-FFI is between r = .66 and r = .85, on average r = .78. Norms: Reference values (M and SD) were obtained in a sample of N = 662 (81% female; age: M = 23, SD = 5.1; range: 18-69 years; non-representative).
sections.Diagnostische Zielsetzung: The BFAS-G is a self-assessment inventory for assessing the Big Five as well as ten underlying aspects and can be used for research and practice.
sections.Aufbau: The BFAS-G comprises 100 items with an administration time of approximately 20 minutes. The following factors and aspects are assessed (aspects in brackets): (1) Extraversion (assertiveness and enthusiasm), (2) Neuroticism (volatility and withdrawal), (3) Agreeableness (compassion and politeness), (4) Conscientiousness (orderliness and industriousness), (5) Intellect/Openness (intellect and openness). An example item reads: "Ich lerne schnell neue Leute kennen."
sections.Grundlagen und Konstruktion: The BFAS-G is the German translation of the Big Five Aspect Scale developed by DeYoung and colleagues (2007). It was examined psychometrically.
sections.Empirische Prüfung und Gütekriterien:
Reliability: Cronbach's alpha is alpha = .71 to alpha = .91.
Validity: The convergent validity with the NEO-FFI is between r = .66 and r = .85, on average r = .78.
Norms: Reference values (means and standard deviations) were obtained in a sample of N = 612 (81% female; age: M = 23, SD = 5.1; range: 18-69 years; non-representative).
sections.Testkonzept/Theoretischer Hintergrund:
The questionnaire Big Five Aspect Scales - German (BFAS-G) is a self-assessment test for assessing the five factors of personality, the so-called Big Five (Goldberg, 1990), as well as ten hierarchically underlying aspects, two per factor. It consists of 100 items.
In a large number of factor-analytic studies in different countries, it has been shown that self- as well as observer assessments of personality can be reduced to five broad factors (e.g. Borgatta, 1964; Borkenau & Ostendorf, 1990; Norman, 1963; Tupes & Christal, 1961). These are the factors extraversion, neuroticism, agreeableness, conscientiousness and openness to experience (Costa & McCrae, 1992).
The structure of personality can best be described by hierarchical models. These postulate one or more broad factors at the top of the model, each with several narrower facets at lower levels. The best-known hierarchical personality model is represented by the NEO Persönlichkeitsinventar nach Costa und McCrae - Revidierte Fassung (NEO-PI-R; Ostendorf & Angleitner, 2004; Costa & McCrae, 1992), which postulates six associated facets for each Big Five factor (for an alternative hierarchical model see also Lee & Ashton, 2004).
DeYoung, Quilty and Peterson (2007) proposed a hierarchical model that postulates two subdimensions, called aspects, for each Big Five factor. These aspects are located at a middle hierarchical level between the five broad factors and the 30 facets of the NEO model. The authors found these aspects in factor-analytic reanalyses of a total of 75 personality facets (15 per Big Five factor) that are assessed in the NEO-PI-R and the AB5C-IPIP (Goldberg, 1999), a freely available questionnaire for assessing the Big Five. The results confirmed that the facets within each factor can be assigned to one of two aspects. This view is in line with the findings of Jang, Livesley, Angleitner, Riemann and Vernon (2002), who found two genetic subfactors within each Big Five factor.
In the next step, DeYoung, Quilty and Peterson (2007) developed an instrument for assessing the ten Big Five aspects. To this end, they selected, on an empirical basis, 100 items from the pool of over 2 000 freely available IPIP items (Goldberg, 1999) that capture these aspects as well as possible and in a discriminating way. These items were translated into German for the BFAS-G.
sections.Testkonzept/Testaufbau:
The BFAS-G consists of 100 items and measures the Big Five with two subscales each. These ten aspects in total are (example items in brackets):
(1) Extraversion
(a) Assertiveness ("Ich übernehme Verantwortung.")
(b) Enthusiasm ("Ich lerne schnell neue Leute kennen.")
(2) Neuroticism
(c) Volatility ("Ich gerate leicht aus der Fassung.")
(d) Withdrawal ("Ich lasse mich schnell entmutigen.")
(3) Agreeableness
(e) Compassion ("Ich habe ein Gespür für die Gefühle anderer.")
(f) Politeness ("Ich setze andere nur selten unter Druck.")
(4) Conscientiousness
(g) Orderliness ("Ich räume meine Sachen stets auf.")
(h) Industriousness ("Ich halte mich an Zeitpläne.")
(5) Intellect/Openness
(i) Intellect ("Es bereitet mir Freude, komplexe Probleme zu lösen.")
(j) Openness ("Kunst ist sehr wichtig für mich.")
Each aspect is assessed with ten items. Accordingly, the Big Five factors are determined via the 20 items of the two associated aspects each. The items are phrased as brief statements. The task of the participant is to indicate to what extent they agree with the respective statement. A seven-point scale is available for this, anchored verbally at three points (from 1 = "trifft überhaupt nicht zu" through 4 = "teils/teils" to 7 = "trifft vollständig zu").
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungsmodus: Negatively keyed items are first reverse-coded (x = 8-i). Subsequently, the items of an aspect or a factor are summed. For the raw test scores, means and standard deviations are given as reference values under "Norming".
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungshilfen: Scoring involves recoding negatively keyed items, calculating sum scores and, if applicable, calculating norm values. Everything can take place script-based. An exemplary SPSS script can be found in the Electronic Test Archive.
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungszeit: As a rule, scoring will be done via Excel or a script and will therefore proceed quickly.
sections.Durchführung/Testformen: The BFAS-G is the German adaptation of the English original of the same name, the BFAS by DeYoung et al. (2007). Testing can be carried out on paper or online - as an individual or group test.
sections.Durchführung/Altersbereiche: The items are suitable for adult persons of any age. Use with adolescents also seems possible, but should be examined first if necessary.
sections.Durchführung/Durchführungszeit: There is no time limit for the test. After 20 minutes most people will be finished.
sections.Durchführung/Material: The test materials available are the questionnaire with the 100 items as well as a syntax file as a scoring aid.
sections.Durchführung/Instruktion: The instruction is standardised. It is on the questionnaire so that it can be read by the participants.
sections.Durchführung/Durchführungsvoraussetzunge: No special qualification is required for administration. The test can also be instructed purely in writing (e.g. online).
sections.Testkonstruktion:
For the original development of the instrument we refer to DeYoung et al. (2007).
We translated the items into German separately. For some of the items, translations by Streib and Wiedmaier (2001) were available, which were also consulted. On this basis, the German items were discussed, selected and, if necessary, modified once more.
The psychometric examination of the BFAS-G was carried out in a sample of 612 persons (81% female; age: M = 23, SD = 5.1; age range: 18-69 years). This is not a population-representative sample.
The item-total correlations at the domain level ranged between rit = .09 and rit = .71 with a median of rit = .47. At the level of the aspects, the item-total correlation coefficients were between rit = .17 and rit = .75 with a median of rit = .55. sections.Gütekriterien/Objektivität: Objectivity of administration and scoring can be assumed to be given.
sections.Gütekriterien/Reliabilität: To estimate reliability, the authors calculated Cronbach's alpha for the five domains and the ten aspects, respectively. The values lie between alpha = .71 and alpha = .91 (see Table 2 under "Test construction").
sections.Gütekriterien/Validität:
In a sample (N = 612, see under "Test construction"), the authors carried out a concurrent validation with the German version of the NEO-FFI (Borkenau & Ostendorf, 2008). The convergent validities at the domain level lie between r = .66 for agreeableness and r = .85 for neuroticism, on average r = .78. Divergent validities, in contrast, are at r = -.06. The aspects of the BFAS also show high associations with the associated domain in the NEO, on average r = .66. The correlation coefficients can be read from Table 3.

sections.Anwendungsmöglichkeiten: The BFAS-G is a self-assessment inventory for assessing the Big Five as well as ten underlying aspects and can be used freely for all research and application purposes, including commercial use.
sections.Bewertung:
The English version of the BFAS-G is a frequently used instrument for assessing the Big Five. One reason for this is probably that the instrument can be used free of licence. In addition, the level of the aspects is of interest for a number of research questions in which, on the one hand, the Big Five are too broad and, on the other hand, existing instruments with facets (such as the NEO-PI-R) are too extensive.
The selection of the items by DeYoung et al. (2007) had the aim of capturing the aspects in the most discriminating way possible. Therefore, items were excluded that loaded equally highly on the two aspects of a factor; such items would, however, possibly be good indicators of the superordinate factor. This has to be taken into account in interpreting the factors, in particular in comparison with other Big Five measurement instruments.
With the designation openness/intellect, the authors proposed a new designation for the fifth Big Five factor, which, for example, Costa and McCrae (1992) called openness to experience, or openness for short. DeYoung et al. (2007) use the same term openness considerably more narrowly, namely for the subordinate aspect that refers to perceptual components such as openness to aesthetics and feelings as well as creativity, and thus exclude the epistemic component (curiosity, enjoyment of thinking, self-assessed intelligence) - a jingle fallacy according to Block (1995).
The aspect intellect has a peculiarity, since seven of the ten items refer to self-assessed abilities (e.g. "Ich habe eine gute Auffassungsgabe."). In contrast, for example, the facet openness to ideas of the NEO-PI-R contains exclusively items on cognitive motivation (e.g. "Ich habe oft Spaß daran, mit Theorien oder abstrakten Ideen zu spielen."). To what extent self-assessed intelligence or even psychometric intelligence is part of the Big Five is discussed controversially (DeYoung, 2011).
